Definition: to mount up; hence, in general, to rise, (figuratively) be majestic
BiblicalUsage: Gaah means to rise up, to mount up, and it carries the sense of triumph. Moses sings it at the Red Sea in Exodus 15:1 — the LORD has triumphed gloriously — and Miriam answers with the same song in Exodus 15:21. Ezekiel uses it for waters that rise until a man cannot pass in Ezekiel 47:5, and Job feels his troubles increasing like a lion rising against him in Job 10:16.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe rising belongs to God first. He rises in triumph over Pharaoh and His river rises until no man can cross it, and I hold that the same God who rose against Egypt rises for His people still.
